mcu_0160_08001178.name: app_main_thunk
mcu_0160_08001178.summary: Tail-call thunk that jumps to the application main entry FUN_0800d548
mcu_0160_08001178.description: Two-instruction veneer that branches to FUN_0800d548, the application main routine that is also the third call in Reset_Handler. It is called from the C-runtime scatter-load routine (mcu_0160_08001a98, the __main equivalent) once RAM sections are initialised. Same role as the VCU image's app_main_thunk.

mcu_0160_08001188.name: Reset_Handler
mcu_0160_08001188.summary: Cortex-M reset vector: system init, C runtime init, then application main
mcu_0160_08001188.description: Reset entry placed in vector slot 1. Calls FUN_0800a2ac (SystemInit-style clock/vector setup), then FUN_08001a98 (Keil __main/scatter-load: copies and decompresses initialised data, zeroes BSS), and finally FUN_0800d548 (application main). The last call is only reached if the scatter-load routine returns; it never returns in normal operation. Identical structure to the VCU Reset_Handler.

mcu_0160_0800119e.name: PendSV_Handler
mcu_0160_0800119e.description: Empty trap: the body is a single branch-to-self, so a PendSV exception hangs the core (until the watchdog resets it). The firmware does not use an RTOS context switch, so PendSV is never expected to fire.

mcu_0160_080011a2.name: Default_Handler
mcu_0160_080011a2.summary: Default trap for unused interrupt vectors: spins forever
mcu_0160_080011a2.description: Single branch-to-self shared by all vector-table slots that have no real handler (the packet lists it under the DMA2_Channel6_7 slot but many slots point at this address). Only PVM, ADC1, CAN1_RX0, CAN1_SE, TMR3 and TMR4 have real handlers on the MCU, so any other interrupt locks the CPU here. Same as VCU Default_Handler.

mcu_0160_08001270.name: __aeabi_memcpy
mcu_0160_08001270.summary: Forward memory copy: word-wise if both pointers 4-byte aligned, else bytewise
mcu_0160_08001270.description: Copies param_3 bytes from param_2 to param_1. If both pointers are word aligned it copies 32-bit words while at least 4 bytes remain, then finishes the tail (or the whole buffer when unaligned) bytewise. No overlap handling (forward copy only), so it is not a memmove. Matches the ARM Compiler runtime __aeabi_memcpy; called from many application routines.

mcu_0160_08001294.name: __aeabi_memset
mcu_0160_08001294.summary: Fill a byte buffer with a constant value (dest, count, value argument order)
mcu_0160_08001294.description: Writes param_3 to param_2 consecutive bytes starting at param_1; a count of 0 does nothing. Note the AEABI argument order (dest, count, value), which is the reverse of C memset; the two small veneers right behind it (mcu_0160_080012a2 and 080012a6) call it, presumably as __aeabi_memclr/memset wrappers.

mcu_0160_08001368.name: __aeabi_fmul
mcu_0160_08001368.summary: Soft-float IEEE-754 single precision multiply (no FPU)
mcu_0160_08001368.description: Multiplies two single-precision floats passed as raw bit patterns. Returns +0 if either operand has a zero magnitude. Otherwise adds exponents (minus bias 0x7f), multiplies the two 24-bit significands in a 64-bit product, normalises with a 1-bit shift if needed, rounds to nearest-even and ORs in the XOR of the signs. Underflow (exponent < 0) flushes to 0; there is no overflow, NaN, infinity or denormal handling. Used heavily by the FOC/control code because the AT32F415 core is integer-only here.
mcu_0160_08001368.notes: Same algorithm as the VCU image's __aeabi_fmul.

mcu_0160_080013cc.name: __ARM_scalbnf
mcu_0160_080013cc.summary: Soft-float scale: add an integer to the exponent of a float (ldexpf style)
mcu_0160_080013cc.description: Returns param_1 * 2^param_2 by adding param_2 to the biased exponent field (param_2 << 23). A zero-magnitude input is returned unchanged; if the new exponent would drop to or below zero the result is flushed to +0. No overflow, NaN or sign-of-zero handling. Used by other soft-float routines and by application code for power-of-two scaling.

mcu_0160_080013f6.name: __aeabi_ui2f
mcu_0160_080013f6.summary: Soft-float convert unsigned 32-bit integer to single-precision float
mcu_0160_080013f6.description: Normalises the integer with a CLZ shift, builds exponent 0x9d - clz (bias 127 + 30 for the position of the top bit) and the top 23 mantissa bits, then rounds to nearest-even using the dropped low bits. Returns 0 for input 0. Despite the decompiler showing a signed parameter, there is no sign handling, so it is the unsigned variant; the signed one is mcu_0160_08001d48.

mcu_12b_080013fe.name: BusFault_Handler_v12b
mcu_12b_080013fe.summary: Bus fault handler in MCU_12b: infinite loop
mcu_12b_080013fe.description: Single branch-to-self trap in the MCU_12b build, installed in the BusFault vector slot. A bus error therefore hangs the CPU until the watchdog resets it. Other builds have the equivalent handler at a different address.

mcu_0160_08001410.name: mcu_q16_mul_round
mcu_0160_08001410.description: Forms the signed 64-bit product of the two arguments and returns bits 16..47 of it, plus 1 if bit 15 is set (round half up). Assuming both operands are Q16 (or one Q16 and one integer) the result keeps the Q16 scale. Single caller mcu_0160_08009598, which also uses the Q30 helpers 08001d6c/08001e0c, i.e. part of one fixed-point calculation.
mcu_0160_08001410.notes: Q-format of the operands is inferred from the shift only.

mcu_12b_0800141e.name: DebugMon_Handler_v12b
mcu_12b_0800141e.summary: Debug monitor exception handler in MCU_12b: empty, returns immediately
mcu_12b_0800141e.description: Empty handler for the DebugMonitor exception vector in the MCU_12b build: it contains only a return. Other builds put the same stub at a different address.

mcu_0160_08001436.name: mcu_get_word_at_0x90
mcu_0160_08001436.summary: Getter returning the 32-bit word at offset 0x90 of a structure
mcu_0160_08001436.description: Returns *(u32 *)(param_1 + 0x90). Only called from mcu_0160_08003f2c, so param_1 is a context/state structure used by that routine; the field's meaning is unknown from this function alone. Present only in the MCU_0160 build.

params.name: param_1
params.description: base address of a struct instance

mcu_0160_08001436.notes: Field purpose unknown; name is positional.

mcu_0160_08001450.name: __aeabi_fdiv
mcu_0160_08001450.summary: Soft-float IEEE-754 single precision divide (no FPU)
mcu_0160_08001450.description: Divides param_1 by param_2 as raw float bits. If either operand has zero magnitude the result is 0 (including division by zero, which does NOT yield infinity). Otherwise subtracts exponents, runs a 24-iteration restoring long division of the significands, computes sign as XOR, applies round-to-nearest-even from the final remainder, and returns 0 when the exponent underflows. No overflow, NaN or denormal handling.

mcu_0160_080016fe.name: __aeabi_ddiv
mcu_0160_080016fe.summary: Soft-float IEEE-754 double precision divide (no FPU)
mcu_0160_080016fe.description: Divides the double in (param_1 lo, param_2 hi) by the double in (param_3 lo, param_4 hi). Returns 0 if either operand is zero. Uses a bitwise restoring long division over the 53-bit significands (20+32 quotient bits), exponent difference with bias 0x3ff, sign XOR, and round-to-nearest-even; underflow returns 0, no overflow, NaN or denormal handling. Result is returned as a 64-bit r0:r1 pair.

returns.description: a/b as double bits (lo in r0, hi in r1)

mcu_0160_080017dc.name: __ARM_scalbn
mcu_0160_080017dc.summary: Soft-float scale: add an integer to the exponent of a double (ldexp style)
mcu_0160_080017dc.description: Returns x * 2^n for a double x in (param_1 lo, param_2 hi) by adding param_3 << 20 to the high word. A zero-magnitude input is returned unchanged; if the exponent would go to zero or below the result is flushed to 0. No overflow/NaN handling. Double-precision counterpart of mcu_0160_080013cc.

mcu_0160_08001824.name: __aeabi_f2iz
mcu_0160_08001824.summary: Soft-float convert single-precision float to signed int, truncating toward zero
mcu_0160_08001824.description: Extracts exponent and 24-bit significand; magnitudes below 1.0 (exponent < 0x7f) give 0, exponents below 0x97 shift the significand right (truncation), larger ones shift left (no saturation, so values >= 2^31 overflow silently). The result is negated if the sign bit of the input is set.

mcu_0160_08001856.name: __aeabi_f2uiz
mcu_0160_08001856.summary: Soft-float convert float magnitude to unsigned int, truncating
mcu_0160_08001856.description: Same extraction as mcu_0160_08001824 (shift significand by 0x96 - exponent, 0 for |x| < 1) but the sign bit is ignored, so negative inputs give their absolute value. Used by a single caller, mcu_0160_080093f8.

mcu_0160_080018bc.name: __aeabi_f2d
mcu_0160_080018bc.summary: Soft-float widen single-precision float to double-precision (r0:r1 pair)
mcu_0160_080018bc.description: Rebases the exponent by +0x380 (1023 - 127), moves the 23-bit fraction to the top of the 52-bit double fraction (>>3 into the high word, low 3 bits into the top of the low word) and keeps the sign. Zero magnitude returns 0.0. Denormals/NaN/Inf are not special-cased.

returns.description: double bits (lo in r0, hi in r1)

mcu_0160_080018e4.name: mcu_fcmp_sortkeys_a
mcu_0160_080018e4.summary: Soft-float compare helper: convert two float bit patterns to comparison keys
mcu_0160_080018e4.description: For each of two 32-bit float words, if it is non-negative as a signed integer it is replaced by 0x80000000 - value; negative words are left unchanged. This is the sign-magnitude-to-ordered-integer step used before comparing floats as integers; returns both transformed values as r0:r1. Identical body to mcu_0160_080018f8; the only caller is mcu_0160_08005830, which probably uses it as the prologue of a float compare (__aeabi_cfcmple/cfrcmple style).

returns.description: transformed (a in r0, b in r1)

mcu_0160_080018e4.notes: Exact AEABI entry point it belongs to is not confirmed; the two copies differ only in address.

mcu_0160_080018f8.name: mcu_fcmp_sortkeys_b
mcu_0160_080018f8.summary: Soft-float compare helper (second copy): convert two float words to comparison keys
mcu_0160_080018f8.description: Byte-for-byte equivalent of mcu_0160_080018e4: any non-negative input word x becomes 0x80000000 - x, negative words pass through, results returned in r0:r1. Called from mcu_0160_08004db8 and mcu_0160_08005830, part of the soft-float comparison cluster. Two copies exist because the ARM runtime emits one per compare entry (e.g. cfcmple vs cfrcmple).

returns.description: transformed (a in r0, b in r1)

mcu_0160_080018f8.notes: Role inferred from the transform, not from the call sites.

mcu_0160_0800190c.name: __aeabi_llsl
mcu_0160_0800190c.description: Shifts the 64-bit value (param_1 low, param_2 high) left by param_3 bits. For shifts of 32 or more only the low word survives, moved into the high word and shifted by param_3-32; otherwise the high word receives the bits carried out of the low word. Used by 64-bit fixed-point code and the soft-float routines.

mcu_0160_0800192a.name: __aeabi_llsr
mcu_0160_0800192a.description: Shifts the 64-bit value (param_1 low, param_2 high) right by param_3 bits with zero fill. For shift >= 32 the result is the high word shifted by param_3-32 with a zero high word; otherwise the low word receives the bits shifted down from the high word.

mcu_0160_0800194a.name: __aeabi_lasr
mcu_0160_0800194a.description: Shifts the signed 64-bit value (param_1 low, param_2 high) right by param_3 with sign fill. For shift >= 32 the low word is the high word arithmetically shifted by param_3-32 and the high word becomes the sign (all 0 or all 1); otherwise the bits move across the word boundary. Only caller is mcu_0160_080014cc.

mcu_0160_08001abc.name: __scatterload_decompress
mcu_0160_08001abc.summary: Decompress a packed section (literals, zero runs, back-references) into RAM
mcu_0160_08001abc.description: ARM/Keil scatter-load decompressor, reached through the load-region table by function pointer (so it has no direct caller). Each token starts with a control byte: low 3 bits = literal count+1 (0 means the count is in the next byte), high nibble = run length (0 means next byte); the literals are copied first. If bit 3 is set the token ends with a copy of (run+2) bytes from the already-written output at distance given by the next byte (LZ77 back-reference), otherwise it emits run zero bytes. Loops until param_2 reaches param_2_start+param_3 and returns 0.
mcu_0160_08001abc.notes: Same algorithm as the VCU image's __scatterload_decompress.

mcu_0160_08001b14.name: mcu_math_cos_q15
mcu_0160_08001b14.summary: Fixed-point cosine: Q15 radians in, Q15 result (sin(x+pi/2))
mcu_0160_08001b14.description: Same algorithm as mcu_0160_08001c54 (sine), but 0x40000000 (pi/2 in the Q31-of-pi phase) is added to the phase first, so it returns cos(x). The input angle is multiplied by 0x517cc1b7 (1/pi in Q32) to get a phase where 2^31 = pi, quadrant-folded, then the top 10 bits index a 513-entry sine table at 0x0800ec20 (step pi/1024) and a second-order interpolation sin(a+d) ~ sin(a) + d*(cos(a) - d*sin(a)/2) is applied using table[i] and table[512-i]. The result is negated for the lower half-plane and rounded to Q15 (+/-32768 = +/-1.0). Only caller: mcu_0160_08006402, probably the Park/inverse-Park transform.
mcu_0160_08001b14.notes: Input/output Q-format inferred from the 1/pi constant and final >>16; table contents not dumped here.

mcu_0160_08001ba0.name: mcu_q15_div_sat
mcu_0160_08001ba0.summary: Fixed-point divide with Q15 result, saturating: (a << 15) / b
mcu_0160_08001ba0.description: Returns a*2^15/b using sign-magnitude long division in steps: it pre-shifts |a| by up to 14 bits (clz limited), divides, then iterates on the remainder shifting in further fractional bits until 15 total bits are produced, truncating toward zero. Division by zero returns 0x7fffffff; if the quotient would overflow it saturates to 0x7fffffff (same signs) or 0x80000000. Called by many control routines (current/voltage normalisation). Companion of the Q30 variant mcu_0160_08001d6c.
mcu_0160_08001ba0.notes: Q15 scale is inferred from the constant 0xf (15) in the shift logic.

mcu_0160_08001c30.name: mcu_q15_mul_sat
mcu_0160_08001c30.summary: Q15 fixed-point multiply with rounding and saturation: (a*b) >> 15
mcu_0160_08001c30.description: Computes the signed 64-bit product, shifts right by 15 with round-half-up (bit 14), and saturates to 0x7fffffff / 0x80000000 if the result does not fit in 32 bits (checks (hi >> 14) + 1 >> 1 != 0). Called throughout the FOC/PI code, e.g. from mcu_0160_08001e5a, 08002b64, 0800480c and 080055c4.
mcu_0160_08001c30.notes: Q-format of the operands is inferred from the shift only.

mcu_0160_08001c54.name: mcu_math_sin_q15
mcu_0160_08001c54.summary: Fixed-point sine: Q15 radians in, Q15 result via 513-entry table with interpolation
mcu_0160_08001c54.description: Multiplies the input by 0x517cc1b7 (1/pi, Q32) and keeps bits 16..47 to get a phase where 2^31 = pi. Bit 30 folds the second quadrant (0x80000000 - phase), bit 31 selects the sign. The top 10 bits of the 31-bit magnitude index the table at 0x0800ec20 (sin(i*pi/1024)); with the fractional angle d = low bits * pi/1024 it evaluates sin(a) + d*(cos(a) - d*sin(a)/2) using table[i] and table[512-i], negates for the sign and rounds to Q15. When the table index is 0 it uses sin(x)~x: (x<<1)*0xc90fcd37 >> 47. Single caller mcu_0160_08006402; companion of mcu_0160_08001b14 (cos).
mcu_0160_08001c54.notes: Input scale deduced from the 1/pi constant: the angle may be a Q15 radian value; the table is not decoded here.

mcu_0160_08001cdc.name: mcu_math_sqrt_fixed
mcu_0160_08001cdc.summary: Fixed-point square root via CLZ normalisation, table seed and two Newton rsqrt steps
mcu_0160_08001cdc.description: Returns in r0 roughly sqrt(param_1 * 2^17) (e.g. a Q15 input gives a Q16 result). Normalises the argument with CLZ, seeds 1/sqrt from a 1024-entry table at 0x0800dc20 indexed by the top 10 bits, refines with two Newton-Raphson steps y' = y*(1.5 - 0.5*x*y^2) in 32x32->high-word arithmetic, multiplies by x to get sqrt, applies a 0xb504f334 (1/sqrt2) factor for odd exponents and shifts back with rounding. Inputs <= 0 (CLZ=0 or 32) return 0. param_2 is passed through in r1 for the zero case; r1 is otherwise an auxiliary value and is ignored by callers. Callers: mcu_0160_08005830, 08006f74, 08007364 (magnitude of d/q vectors etc.).

returns.description: low word = sqrt result, high word = scratch

mcu_0160_08001cdc.notes: Output scaling derived from the shift constants (+15); the 143/12b variant uses +2 instead.

mcu_0160_08001d48.name: __aeabi_i2f
mcu_0160_08001d48.summary: Soft-float convert signed 32-bit integer to single-precision float
mcu_0160_08001d48.description: Returns 0 for 0; otherwise takes the sign, negates negative inputs, normalises with CLZ and builds the float from sign, exponent 0x8f - clz (clz-adjusted, one lower than the unsigned version because the magnitude is up to 31 bits) and the 23 top mantissa bits. Truncates instead of rounding. Callers include mcu_0160_08002b64 and 08004db8.
mcu_0160_08001d48.notes: Mantissa is truncated, not rounded to nearest-even.

mcu_143_08001d50.name: mcu_q28_mul
mcu_143_08001d50.description: Signed 64-bit product shifted right by 28 (low word >> 28 plus high word << 4), no rounding or saturation. Only present in MCU_12b and MCU_143; its single caller is mcu_143_0800a580, which also uses mcu_143_08001d60. The later builds use other Q formats.
mcu_143_08001d50.notes: Q-format inferred from the shift only.

mcu_143_08001d60.name: mcu_math_sqrt_fixed_v143
mcu_143_08001d60.summary: Fixed-point square root, MCU_12b/143 variant (table at 0x0800da48)
mcu_143_08001d60.description: Same algorithm as mcu_0160_08001cdc (CLZ normalise, table seed, two Newton rsqrt iterations, 1/sqrt2 for odd exponent) but the output scale constant is +2 instead of +15 and the seed table is at 0x0800da48, so the result is sqrt(param_1 * 2^30) (a different Q format than the 0160 build). Inputs <= 0 return 0 with param_2 in r1. Single caller mcu_143_0800a580.
mcu_143_08001d60.notes: Scale derived from shift constants only.

mcu_0160_08001d6c.name: mcu_q30_div_sat
mcu_0160_08001d6c.summary: Fixed-point divide with Q30 result, saturating: (a << 30) / b
mcu_0160_08001d6c.description: Same long-division scheme as mcu_0160_08001ba0 but producing 30 fractional bits (clz limited to 0x1e). Division by zero returns 0x7fffffff; overflow saturates to 0x7fffffff or 0x80000000 depending on sign agreement; result truncates toward zero. Single caller mcu_0160_08009598.

mcu_0160_08001dfc.name: mcu_q30_mul
mcu_0160_08001dfc.description: Signed 64-bit product shifted right 30 bits (low word >> 30 plus high word * 4), no rounding. Callers: mcu_0160_08001e5a and mcu_0160_0800767c. The rounding twin is mcu_0160_08001e0c.
mcu_0160_08001dfc.notes: Q-format inferred from the shift only.

mcu_0160_08001e0c.name: mcu_q30_mul_round
mcu_0160_08001e0c.description: Like mcu_0160_08001dfc but adds 1 when bit 29 of the low product word is set (round half up). Callers: mcu_0160_08005240, 0800705c, 080093f8 and 08009598.
mcu_0160_08001e0c.notes: Q-format inferred from the shift only.
